Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. Priya Punia and Smriti Mandhana will open the innings for India Women. Marufa Akter will start with the new ball for Bangladesh Women. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, India Women will be certainly the happier side at the halfway mark. They are on course to take a 1-0 lead in the series. On the other hand, Bangladesh Women need a miraculous bowling effort to defend this total. Can their bowlers make a match out of this? Let's find out. Back in a bit for the chase...

As far as Bangladesh are concerned, it has been a disappointing batting effort from them. At the start, the two Bangladesh openers found themselves struggling against the new ball. This pressure of dot balls took a toll on them who departed in quick succession. Just when Fargana Hoque and Nigar Sultana were starting to find their feet, rain arrived and hampered their momentum. That said, Fargana Hoque got herself going with a couple of boundaries after the resumption but could not carry on. Nigar Sultana showed a fight but fell 11 runs short of her fifty. Towards the end, contributions from Fahima Khatun and Sultana Khatun helped Bangladesh Women cross 150.

The Indian bowlers have vindicated their skipper's decision to bowl first and how! A clinical effort by the bowling unit has helped India Women restrict Bangladesh Women to 152. After Harmanpreet Kaur called it right and won the toss, India's new ball bowlers were on the money right from ball one and did not allow Bangladesh to settle in. Playing in her maiden ODI game, Amanjot Kaur set the tone for India Women with her maiden ODI wicket. The rest of the bowling unit chipped in as well and continued to mount the pressure on Bangladesh Women. India Women kept taking wickets at regular intervals and never allowed Bangladesh Women to forge big partnerships. Amanjot Kaur was the chief wrecker with four wickets.

OUT! RUN-OUT! Quicker and flatter outside off, Fahima Khatun cuts it to the fielder at short third man and runs for it. Devika Vaidya was quick to collect the ball and throw it straight at the stumps for a run-out. Devika Vaidya does superbly as she inflicts a run out here. The Bangladesh Women's innings come to a close at 152 runs as Shorna Akter will not walk out to bat as she is retired hurt.

Update - 11.35 am IST (6.05 am GMT) - Some positive news! Live pictures show that the rain has relented at the Shere Bangla National Stadium. The ground staff have made their way out to the middle and are in the process of removing water from the covers before taking them off the square.
Update - 11.03 am IST (5.33 am GMT) - The waiting game continues! Rain continues to pour down and the covers are firmly in place. Stay tuned for further updates.

Update - 10.28 am IST (4.58 am GMT) - Just when the ground staff were in the process of removing the covers, the rain returned and the entire square is covered once again. Seems like we will have to wait a little longer.

Update - 10.18 am IST (4.48 am GMT) - It has started to rain and the umpires have asked the ground staff to bring on the covers. The entire square has been covered now. Let's hope this is just a passing shower. We will keep you posted.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to start as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. India Women are seen in a huddle near the ropes before they disperse. Sharmin Akhter and Murshida Khatun will open the innings for Bangladesh Women. Pooja Vastrakar has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings for India Women. Off we go...

Nigar Sultana, the captain of Bangladesh Women, says they would have bowled first but the track seems good so they would want to bat well. Adds that the momentum will prove key for the side. Informs that Shorna Akter is debuting for the side today.

Harmanpreet Kaur, the skipper of India Women, says they would like to bowl first as the conditions are overcast and that will help the pacers early on. Adds that the team that plays the best cricket will win. Informs that Amanjot Kaur and Bareddy Anusha are debuting for the country.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Priya Punia, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Yastika Bhatia (WK), Deepti Sharma, Amanjot Kaur (On ODI Debut), Pooja Vastrakar, Sneh Rana, Devika Vaidya, Bareddy Anusha (On ODI debut).

Bangladesh Women (Playing XI) - Nigar Sultana (C/WK), Nahida Akter, Ritu Moni, Shorna Akter (On ODI debut), Murshida Khatun, Fahima Khatun, Marufa Akter, Fargana Hoque, Sultana Khatun, Rabeya Khan, Sharmin Akhter.
TOSS-: India Women have won the toss and elected to BOWL first.

Update - 8.44 am IST (3.14 am GMT) - Uh oh! Not the news any of us would have wanted to start the day with. Showers early in the morning have meant that the outfield is wet. Toss has been delayed for now and the covers are on as well. Let's hope this is only a brief delay.

Bangladesh Women on the other hand would be stepping into this game on a positive note as they defeated India Women in the final game of the T20 series and that would have uplifted the confidence amongst the squad sky high. The batting would be dependent on skipper Nigar Sultana, Sultana Khatun and Shamima Sultana while Rabeya Khan and Fahima Khatun would lead the bowling attack. The side that wins the battle against the spin attack would probably have the upper hand in this fixture. Let's see what unfolds in a while. Stay tuned for toss and team updates...

India Women is carrying happy memories into the ODI series after clinching the T20I series 2-1 against the hosts. The team is a perfect blend of experience and youth with skipper Harmanpreet Kaur leading the side in an exemplary way. The team will be relying on star batters Smriti Mandhana and her partner in crime Shafali Verma for a solid start on which players like Jemimah Rodrigues, skipper Harmanpreet Kaur and the rest could pounce upon. The bowling department would be loaded on the shoulders of Meghna Singh, and Pooja Vastrakar, and the all-around ability of Deepti Sharma would be an X-factor for the side.

Hello and a very warm welcome to everyone tuning in. It is now time for the ODI series between the two Asian neighboring countries as India Women takes on Bangladesh Women. All the games of this 3-match ODI series will be played at the Shere Bangla National Stadium, Mirpur, Dhaka.
...MATCH DAY...

India Women bagged the recently concluded three-match T20I series and now we move into the ODIs which have much higher stakes for Bangladesh Women as ICC Women's Championship points are on offer. Ten teams are fighting for the five places for direct entry in the 2025 World Cup, but India Women have already qualified as hosts and they will look to just keep the momentum going while the hosts are struggling at the bottom and are in desperate need of the points. The first ODI of the three will be played at the Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium. Bangladesh have a decent batting line-up with Shamima Sultana and Salma Khatun as the openers while skipper Nigar Sultana will have a major responsibility to score the runs. Sobhana Mostary, Fargana Hoque, and Nahida Akter form a strong middle order. Marufa Akter and Ritu Moni will lead their pace attack with the likes of Lata Mondal for company. They have a good line-up of spinners with Salma Khatun, Fahima Khatun, and Rabeya Khan in the team who caused serious trouble to Indian batters in the T20Is recently and will be key again, and they can also score some runs in the lower order as well which is a plus for the hosts. India, on the other hand, have a very experienced side and will be favourites. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana will look to give them the starts again while Harmanpreet Kaur, Harleen Deol, and Jemimah Rodrigues will be the key batters in the middle order. Pooja Vastrakar and Meghna Singh will lead the pace attack with Deepti Sharma being crucial with her all-round abilities. They have a good all-around attack with a flurry of spinners in case any need arises. We can surely expect an exciting game of cricket. Let's see who takes the lead in the series.
